page.title: Integrations
page.guideSubject: store connections, API tokens and MCP

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.copyDescription: This is the only time the token is shown. Store it somewhere safe. You will not see it again.
tokens.copyFailed: Copy failed. Select the token above and copy it manually.
tokens.formDescription: Use a token to authenticate scripts and the MCP server with a Bearer header. Limits are per workspace, so a second token adds no capacity.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.scopeHint: Read only is the safer default. Choose read and write for a script that changes data, or for an agent you allow to track keywords, manage competitors and update actions.
tokens.loadFailed: API tokens could not be loaded.
tokens.empty: No tokens yet. Create one to authenticate scripts or the MCP server with a Bearer header.
tokens.note: {count} · Limits are per workspace, so a second token adds no capacity.
tokens.noteExpired: {count}, {expired} expired · Limits are per workspace, so a second token adds no capacity.
tokens.revokeBody: Anything using {name} will stop authenticating immediately. This cannot be undone.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.connectDescription: Name a token for this agent. We mint it read-only unless you allow changes, and show you the ready-to-paste connect snippets.
mcp.allowChanges: Allow this agent to make changes
mcp.changesHint: Adds tools that track and untrack keywords, add and remove competitors, and change the status of actions. A token that can make changes can change anything through the API too, so keep it private.
mcp.tokenNoticeRead: The token is read-only and is shown once. Copy what you need before closing.
mcp.tokenNoticeWrite: The token can make changes and is shown once. Copy what you need before closing, and keep it private.
mcp.hostedDescription: Your client connects straight to this instance. Nothing to install.
mcp.localDescription: For a checkout of the repository. Hosted users need nothing here.
mcp.copyFailed: Copy failed. Select the text and copy it manually.
mcp.footer: Every connection is authenticated with a personal API token.
mcp.description: Point any MCP client at this instance to ask about your apps, keywords, rankings and audits in plain language. Tools are read-only unless you allow an agent to make changes when you connect it.

storeConnections.ownerOnly: Only the workspace owner can connect a store.
storeConnections.off: Store connections are off on this instance. Set STORE_CONNECT_ENCRYPTION_KEY to turn them on.

appStore.beforeRole: You need the Account Holder or Admin role in App Store Connect to create a team key.
appStore.beforeTime: It takes about five minutes, and Apple lets you download the key file only once.
appStore.beforeNumbers: The first numbers appear one or two days after you connect.
appStore.empty: No store connected. Connect App Store Connect to see impressions, product page views, Get taps and conversion by market, and to post review replies from the reviews page.
appStore.noApps: Import an App Store app to read its numbers through this key.
appStore.refused: App Store Connect refused this key. Verify it again, or connect a new key.
appStore.waiting: Waiting for Apple's first report, usually within two days of connecting.
appStore.disconnect: AsoBeast deletes the stored key and stops downloading reports. The numbers already stored are kept and appear again once you connect a key. Revoke the key in App Store Connect too if you no longer need it.

states.stopped: Stopped by Apple, verify to request again

googlePlay.beforeOwner: You need Owner or Admin access to the Play Console developer account.
googlePlay.beforeBucket: Copy the bucket id from Download reports in Play Console first.
googlePlay.beforeTime: It takes about ten minutes, and Google can take up to two days to apply a new service account's access.
googlePlay.empty: Not connected. Connect the Google Play Console to see store listing visitors, acquisitions and conversion by market and installs per search term, and to post review replies from the reviews page.
googlePlay.noApps: Import a Google Play app to read its numbers through this connection.
googlePlay.refused: Google refused this connection. Check its access in Play Console, verify it again, or reconnect.
googlePlay.waiting: Waiting for the first store performance file, which Google writes to the bucket once a day.
googlePlay.disconnect: AsoBeast deletes the stored service account key or Google sign in and stops reading the bucket. The numbers already stored are kept and appear again once you reconnect. Delete the key in Google Cloud, or remove AsoBeast under Third party connections in your Google account, if you no longer need it.

storeConnections.replyRoleAppStore: This App Store Connect key cannot respond to reviews. Connect a key with the Admin or Customer Support role.
storeConnections.replyRoleGoogle: This service account cannot reply to reviews. Give it the Reply to reviews permission in Play Console.
storeConnections.googleSignInCannotReply: This Google sign in was not allowed to manage Play Console, so it cannot post replies. Sign in with Google again and allow it, or connect a service account key with the Reply to reviews permission. If you already allowed it, give your Google account the Reply to reviews permission in Play Console.

summary.nothingConnected: No store connected yet. Connect one to see the store funnel beside your rankings.

connectAppStore.description: Create a team key with the Admin role in Users and Access, Integrations, so AsoBeast can ask Apple for the reports. AsoBeast checks it with Apple, stores it encrypted and never shows it again.
connectAppStore.issuerRequired: Paste the issuer ID shown above the team keys in App Store Connect.
connectAppStore.keyIdRequired: The key ID is ten letters and digits.
connectAppStore.privateKeyRequired: Paste the whole contents of the .p8 file, or choose the file.
connectAppStore.connectFailed: Could not connect App Store Connect.
connectAppStore.keyNote: Paste the key or choose the .p8 file you downloaded. A team key with the Admin role covers reports and replies; Sales and Reports reads reports only, Customer Support replies only.

connectPlay.googleDescription: Sign in with the Google account that owns your Play Console developer account. AsoBeast asks Google for read only access to Cloud Storage and for access to Play Console to post the review replies you send, checks the bucket and stores the sign in encrypted.
connectPlay.keyDescription: Use a Google Cloud service account invited in Play Console under Users and permissions, with View app information and download bulk reports on the Account permissions tab, and Reply to reviews to post replies. AsoBeast checks it with Google, stores the key encrypted and never shows it again.
connectPlay.bucketRequired: Copy the bucket id that starts with pubsite_prod from Download reports in Play Console.
connectPlay.keyRequired: Choose the JSON key file Google Cloud downloaded for the service account, or paste its contents.
connectPlay.connectFailed: Could not connect the Google Play Console.
connectPlay.bucketNote: Play Console shows it under Download reports, as the Cloud Storage URI after gs://.

serviceAccount.label: Service account key
serviceAccount.placeholder: Contents of the downloaded JSON key
serviceAccount.note: Choose the JSON key file or paste its contents. AsoBeast reads only the store performance files in the bucket, and posts only the review replies you send.

playSignIn.cancelledBody: Nothing was connected. Start again from store connections when you are ready.
playSignIn.incompleteBody: Google did not return the code AsoBeast needs. Start the sign in again from store connections.
playSignIn.failedBody: Could not finish the Google sign in. Try again from store connections.
playSignIn.connectingBody: Checking the bucket with your Google account.
